content:
After months away from the spotlight, Ariana Grande is back on television. The singer crashed Jimmy Fallon's monologue on The Tonight Show on Sunday night, November 8, alongside her Focker-in-Law co-stars Robert De Niro and Ben Stiller, in her first major TV appearance since stepping back from public life in September.

The trio joined forces to sing "O Christmas Tree," with Grande and Stiller trading lines back and forth before De Niro lip-synched the final line — the punchline landing as the two-time Oscar winner sounded like a shockingly good singer. The appearance came on a rare Sunday episode of The Tonight Show, a special that followed the Sunday Night Football game between the Chicago Bears and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

All three stars also sat down for an interview about the comedy sequel, the fourth installment in the Meet the Parents series and the follow-up to 2010's Little Fockers. They played a round of True Confessions and starred in a skit parodying soap operas. Until Sunday, it had been unclear how much Grande would take part in the film's promotional tour.

In the film, Grande plays Olivia Jones, the girlfriend of Henry Focker — Greg and Pam's now-grown son, played by Skyler Gisondo. Olivia is a life coach and a former FBI hostage negotiator, and Henry plans to propose to her. Greg, played by Stiller, is convinced his future daughter-in-law is hiding something, and sets out to unmask her over a weekend celebrating Jack Byrnes' 80th birthday. The film is written and directed by John Hamburg, who co-wrote the three previous films. It opens in theaters November 25, 2026 — Thanksgiving Eve — from Universal Pictures in the United States and Canada, with Paramount Pictures handling international release.

Grande said she was "so honored" to be asked to star in the film, which marks her first film role since she played Glinda in the two-part Wicked movie adaptation. She also reminisced about taking a selfie with De Niro backstage at The Tonight Show in 2015 and working with Stiller on Zoolander 2.

The 33-year-old star has kept a low profile since concluding her Eternal Sunshine Tour on September 1, a 41-date run. A month before the tour ended, her representatives announced she would be "taking a step back from visibility," calling it "a much-deserved break from public-facing work and appearances which has led to endless, ongoing public scrutiny." Speaking to a Chicago concert crowd the following day, Grande said the decision was "not a reactive or impulsive thing" but one that came from "a thoughtful and empowered place." She later bowed out of a planned West End debut in a summer 2027 production of Sunday in the Park with George alongside Wicked co-star Jonathan Bailey; the production was scrapped in September.

Analysis: A comeback timed to the Thanksgiving box office

Sunday night answered the open question hanging over Universal's holiday release: Grande is in for the promotional push. Her appearance was not a quiet return — it was a Christmas carol sung shoulder to shoulder with two of the biggest names in comedy, on a special Sunday-night broadcast built to draw a football-sized audience. For a franchise returning after 16 years, that is the kind of launch money cannot buy. It also marks a careful re-entry for a star who set a boundary in August and has kept it: one high-profile night, tied directly to the work, with the film — not the gossip — as the reason she showed up. If the box office follows the buzz, the Fockers' Thanksgiving return could be one of the season's biggest comedies.
